items.title: How much does a good catalog match actually save, versus a poor one?
items.description: L3's order-notification system was estimated at ~120 engineer-hours to design a reliable, replayable notification system from a blank page. The transactional outbox pattern matched every one of its constraints (a 'good fit' — see the fit table). Drag match quality down toward 'poor fit' — a problem that only superficially resembles the catalog entry's assumptions — and watch how little of that 120-hour cost the pattern actually removes once the shape doesn't really line up.

params.name: matchQuality
params.label: How closely the problem matches the pattern's assumptions

params.name: teamFamiliarity
params.label: Team's existing familiarity with the pattern

items.compute: const fromScratchHours = 120; const learningCurveHours = ((100 - params.teamFamiliarity) / 100) * 40; const remainingDesignHours = ((100 - params.matchQuality) / 100) * fromScratchHours; const hoursWithPattern = remainingDesignHours + learningCurveHours; const hoursSaved = Math.max(0, Math.round(fromScratchHours - hoursWithPattern)); return { hoursSaved };

outputs.label: Engineer-hours saved versus designing from scratch
